edges.description: Loss of functional KLKB1 product removes prekallikrein activity from plasma. In the usual quantitative defect the antigen falls with it.
The laboratory phenotype is the direct measurement of this plasma state, by coagulant activity and by antigen.
Kallikrein is the enzyme that activates further factor XII, so without the zymogen there is no kallikrein to close that loop.
edges.target: Loss of Kallikrein Feedback Activation of Factor XII

edges.description: Kallikrein is also the protease that cleaves high-molecular-weight kininogen, so deficient plasma cannot release bradykinin on contact activation.

Kallikrein activates pro-urokinase and contributes to contact-activated plasmin generation, so deficient plasma lyses fibrin more slowly after surface activation. The intermediates are the urokinase and plasminogen activation steps.
With the amplifier gone, surface autoactivation of factor XII is the only way into the pathway, which makes contact activation slow rather than absent.
edges.source: Loss of Kallikrein Feedback Activation of Factor XII
edges.target: Rate-Limited Factor XII Autoactivation as the Sole Contact Trigger

edges.description: The aPTT reagent initiates clotting by contact activation, so an assay that depends on the rate of factor XII activation is prolonged when the kallikrein amplifier is missing.
edges.source: Rate-Limited Factor XII Autoactivation as the Sole Contact Trigger

edges.description: Because factor XII still autoactivates, factor XI and factor IX are still reached and thrombin is still generated in vivo. The known intermediates are the factor XI and factor IX activation steps.
edges.source: Rate-Limited Factor XII Autoactivation as the Sole Contact Trigger
edges.target: Hemostasis Preserved Despite the Contact Defect

edges.description: In mice, the lower bradykinin tone that follows prekallikrein deletion runs through compensating vasoprotective signalling, with increased Mas receptor expression and plasma prostacyclin, and ends in delayed arterial thrombosis.
edges.target: Reduced Kallikrein-Driven Thromboinflammation in Model Systems

edges.description: Proposed, not established. Bradykinin is a vasodilator, so losing its kallikrein-dependent production has been offered as the reason reported patients carry an excess of hypertension. No study has measured blood pressure against bradykinin or kinin-receptor signalling in deficient patients, and prekallikrein-null mice are normotensive, so the intermediates are unknown and the edge belongs to the hypothesis group rather than to the established chain.

edges.target: Hemostasis Preserved Despite the Contact Defect

edges.source: Preoperative Fresh Frozen Plasma for Activated Clotting Time Monitoring
edges.target: Rate-Limited Factor XII Autoactivation as the Sole Contact Trigger

edges.description: Knockout plasma shows the defining kinetic signature of the human defect, a long aPTT and defective contact-activation-induced thrombin generation that partially corrects when incubation is prolonged.
edges.limitations: Mouse and human contact-factor biology are not identical, and the correction is reported as partial rather than quantified against human plasma.
edges.target: Rate-Limited Factor XII Autoactivation as the Sole Contact Trigger

edges.description: The knockout does not bleed abnormally in provoked challenges, matching the human phenotype, but the match is not exact: tail bleeding time was modestly increased, while renal bleeding times were unaffected.
edges.limitations: Murine tail and renal bleeding assays are not human surgery, and the modest tail-bleeding increase has no human counterpart, so the agreement is qualitative.
edges.target: Hemostasis Preserved Despite the Contact Defect

edges.description: Arterial occlusion is prevented or delayed across ferric chloride and rose bengal models, and the protection extends to thromboinflammatory and atherosclerotic models. This is the model's distinctive finding and the node is scoped to model systems because of it.
edges.limitations: The human disease shows no such protection: nine of 75 reported patients had thrombotic events, and reported patients carry an excess rather than a deficit of cardiovascular disease. The fidelity tier is low for that reason, not because the murine result is weak.
edges.target: Reduced Kallikrein-Driven Thromboinflammation in Model Systems

nodes.description: Kaolin-activated plasmin generation and fibrinolysis are slow in deficient plasma and correct on adding prekallikrein, because kallikrein activates pro-urokinase and contributes to contact-dependent plasminogen activation. In patients, reported fibrinolysis has been normal or defective rather than consistently impaired, and testing of one deficient sibling concluded that prekallikrein is not important for fibrinolysis in vivo, where tissue and vessel-wall activators do the work. The node is therefore kept as an in vitro finding and no clinical consequence is claimed for it.

evidence.reference_title: Fletcher factor deficiency. A diminished rate of Hageman factor activation caused by absence of prekallikrein with abnormalities of coagulation, fibrinolysis, chemotactic activity, and kinin generation.
evidence.snippet: It also possesses a diminished rate of kaolin-activable coagulation and fibrinolysis and possesses a defect in kaolin-activable chemotactic activity.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital prekallikrein deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Kallikrein can mainly affect the formation of bradykinin from high-molecular-weight kininogen and the activation of pro-urokinase to urokinase.

evidence.reference_title: Multiple cerebral thrombosis in Fletcher factor (prekallikrein) deficiency: a case report.
evidence.snippet: Prekallikrein deficiency is found not to be important in normal in vivo fibrinolysis, which possibly operates via tissue or vessel wall fibrinolytic activator release.

nodes.description: Thrombin generation after injury is unaffected, both because the tissue factor and factor VIIa route is untouched and because the contact pathway is slowed rather than blocked. Patients come through major operations without hemostatic support, and whole-blood viscoelastic testing, which also depends on contact activation, can be entirely normal in the same patient whose plasma aPTT is doubled or tripled. This node is why an alarming laboratory value has no hemorrhagic consequence. The extrinsic-pathway binding names the route that stays intact, and it carries no modifier because that route's activity is unchanged.
nodes.id: Hemostasis Preserved Despite the Contact Defect

animal_models.description: The knockout does not bleed abnormally in provoked challenges, matching the human phenotype, but the match is not exact: tail bleeding time was modestly increased, while renal bleeding times were unaffected.
animal_models.name: Plasma prekallikrein-deficient mouse

biological_processes: tissue factor and factor VIIa initiated coagulation, unaffected

evidence.reference_title: Normal thromboelastography with a markedly prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time in severe prekallikrein deficiency: Implications for perioperative hemostatic assessment.
evidence.snippet: Severe PK deficiency may markedly prolong the plasma-based aPTT without parallel abnormalities on TEG 6s, highlighting assay-specific differences in sensitivity to PK deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Normal thromboelastography with a markedly prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time in severe prekallikrein deficiency: Implications for perioperative hemostatic assessment.
evidence.snippet: The patient underwent surgery without hemostatic complications or transfusion.

evidence.reference_title: Rare Prekallikrein Deficiency Identified During Workup of Isolated Prolonged Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time.
evidence.snippet: However, a contact factor (ie, factor XII, prekallikrein, and high molecular weight kininogen) deficiency, which may also cause a prolonged aPTT, is not associated with clinical bleeding.

nodes.description: Reported patients carry an excess of hypertension and of its vascular complications, which is the one clinical association that has repeatedly been noticed. Across all 89 published cases of proven deficiency, hypertension or a vascular complication of it was found in 21 patients, 21 of the 64 aged over 25 years. No frequency band is recorded, because the two denominators fall in different bands and hypertension is age-dependent, so a single figure for the disease would be a guess. In the assembled cohort of 111 cases, cardiovascular events occurred in 15 per cent overall and rose with age across bands. Whether the association is causal is unsettled: these are analyses of reported cases with no matched comparison group, the authors who describe it say explicitly that association is not causation, and prekallikrein-null mice are normotensive. It is recorded as a phenotype because it is a consistent observation, not because a mechanism is established.

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence of hypertension and its complications in congenital prekallikrein deficiency: analysis of all reported cases and clinical significance.
evidence.snippet: Altogether, 89 cases of proven prekallikrein deficiency have been described in the literature. Hypertension or vascular complications of it were found in 21 patients

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence of hypertension and its complications in congenital prekallikrein deficiency: analysis of all reported cases and clinical significance.
evidence.snippet: If the analysis is limited to patients over 25 years of age, the number becomes 21 out of 64 cases (38.2%).

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence of hypertension and its complications in congenital prekallikrein deficiency: analysis of all reported cases and clinical significance.
evidence.snippet: This prevalence is much higher than that seen for other conditions occasionally found in patients with prekallikrein deficiency, namely hyperthyroidism, lupus erythematosus, chronic lymphocytic leukemia, kidney malformation, peptic ulcer, and myelofibrosis (1-2%).

evidence.reference_title: Cardiovascular diseases in congenital prekallikrein deficiency: comparison with other chance-associated morbidities.
evidence.snippet: The significance of these findings is critically discussed as association between two diseases does not necessarily indicate the existence of a causative relation between the two.

evidence.reference_title: Severe plasma prekallikrein deficiency: Clinical characteristics, novel KLKB1 mutations, and estimated prevalence.
evidence.snippet: The prevalence of cardiovascular events was 15% (6% <40 years; 21% 40-65 years; 33% >65 years) for an annualized rate of 0.4%.

meta.association: Biallelic loss-of-function variants, predominantly truncating (nonsense and frameshift) with a minority of missense alleles that either block secretion or leave a non-functional circulating protein; reported variants cluster in the exons encoding the catalytic domain

evidence.reference_title: Severe plasma prekallikrein deficiency: Clinical characteristics, novel KLKB1 mutations, and estimated prevalence.
evidence.snippet: We characterized the genetic background of severe PK deficiency, critically appraised mutations, and provided prevalence estimates.

evidence.reference_title: A Case of Severe Prekallikrein Deficiency Manifesting as Isolated Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT) Prolongation.
evidence.snippet: PK deficiency is thought to be caused by mutations in the KLKB1 gene, which is located on chromosome 4q35 and inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern

meta.frequency: the only known cause of inherited prekallikrein deficiency

nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous KLKB1 variants abolish production of functional prekallikrein. The reported spectrum is dominated by truncating alleles, with nonsense, frameshift and missense classes all represented and a concentration in the exons encoding the catalytic domain. Missense alleles act by two routes: some prevent secretion of the protein, while others leave a circulating but non-functional molecule.

evidence.reference_title: A structure-function analysis in patients with prekallikrein deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The total number of missense mutation was 10, together with 3 stop codons and 2 insertions. These mutations involved mainly exons 11 and 14.

evidence.reference_title: [Severe prekallikrein deficiency due to a compound heterozygosis in the KLKB1-gene].
evidence.snippet: The prekallikrein deficiency results from two mutations in the KLKB 1-gene: first, an insertion of 1 bp in codon 149 in exon 5 and, second, a base exchange Cys 548 (TGC) > Tyr (TAC) in exon 14.

nodes.description: On a negatively charged surface, factor XII first autoactivates, converts prekallikrein to kallikrein, and kallikrein then activates much more factor XII. That reciprocal step is the amplifier of the contact phase, and it is what prekallikrein deficiency removes.
nodes.id: Loss of Kallikrein Feedback Activation of Factor XII

evidence.reference_title: Fletcher factor deficiency. A diminished rate of Hageman factor activation caused by absence of prekallikrein with abnormalities of coagulation, fibrinolysis, chemotactic activity, and kinin generation.
evidence.snippet: Although the Hageman factor-dependent pathways appear to be initiated by contact activation of Hageman factor, the kallikrein generated activates more Hageman factor; this feedback is necessary for the Hageman factor-dependent pathways to proceed at a normal rate.

evidence.reference_title: Normal thromboelastography with a markedly prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time in severe prekallikrein deficiency: Implications for perioperative hemostatic assessment.
evidence.snippet: PK is converted to kallikrein by FXIIa, and kallikrein in turn activates additional FXII, amplifying the contact process

nodes.description: No replacement or prophylaxis is needed, including before surgery. The management decision is to withhold treatment: reported patients have undergone hallux amputation, kidney biopsy, deep brain stimulator implantation and endovascular aortic repair without hemorrhagic complications, several of them after fresh frozen plasma given for the laboratory value rather than for any hemostatic need, and reviews of the accumulated cases conclude that routine blood-product prophylaxis is not indicated. The point of recognising the deficiency is to allow a definitive assessment of bleeding risk and so avoid deferring the procedure.

evidence.reference_title: A Case of Severe Prekallikrein Deficiency Manifesting as Isolated Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT) Prolongation.
evidence.snippet: Our review suggests that routine prophylactic administration of blood products for pre-operative management of this condition is not indicated but may be considered if the patient is at high risk of hemorrhage or clinical deterioration.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnostic Pearls and Clinical Implications of Prekallikrein Deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Our case further highlights the clinical pearls for diagnosis and further endorses that these patients can safely undergo surgical procedures without the need for plasma transfusions or factor concentrate usage.

evidence.reference_title: Rare Prekallikrein Deficiency Identified During Workup of Isolated Prolonged Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time.
evidence.snippet: Identification of a contact factor deficiency is clinically useful information, as it allows for a definitive assessment of bleeding risk.

nodes.description: Plasma prekallikrein activity is absent or near-absent. This is the measured biochemical state that defines the disease, and in most patients it is the only abnormality that can be found. Immunological testing splits the deficiency in two: cross-reactive-material-negative cases, roughly 70 per cent of the total, have no detectable antigen, while cross-reactive-material-positive cases carry a non-functional molecule at reduced but measurable concentration.

evidence.reference_title: Heterogeneity of human prekallikrein deficiency (Fletcher trait): evidence that five of 18 cases are positive for cross-reacting material.
evidence.snippet: In the five other subjects, however, nonfunctional material immunologically indistinguishable from normal prekallikrein was detected by radioimmunoassays at concentrations of 13 to 30 per cent (CRM+ variant).

evidence.reference_title: Congenital prekallikrein deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Immunological studies allow differentiation into two types, namely cases of true deficiency, which are approximately 70% of the total, and cases with abnormal forms.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization of a variant prekallikrein, prekallikrein Long Beach, from a family with mixed cross-reacting material-positive and cross-reacting material-negative prekallikrein deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The variant was cleaved by beta-Factor XIIa 200 times slower than the normal molecule, and no amidolytic activity was detected for the cleaved variant.

nodes.description: The engineered knockout is the only substantial model of this disease and it reproduces the human biochemistry closely, including the prolonged aPTT and its partial correction on prolonged incubation. It diverges from the human disease where it is most interesting, in being strongly protected from thrombosis.

evidence.reference_title: Effects of plasma kallikrein deficiency on haemostasis and thrombosis in mice: murine ortholog of the Fletcher trait.
evidence.snippet: Deficiency in humans is characterised by prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT); however, the balance between thrombosis and haemostasis is not fully understood.

nodes.description: The one stated indication for replacement is not hemostasis but repair of a monitoring assay. The activated clotting time used to steer intraoperative heparin and protamine is contact activated and so is already prolonged at baseline in these patients, which makes it unusable. Replenishing prekallikrein with fresh frozen plasma before the procedure restored a usable activated clotting time during endovascular aortic repair. This is a single reported case and the indication is narrow: elsewhere fresh frozen plasma has been given for the laboratory value alone, which is the practice the preceding record argues against.
nodes.id: Preoperative Fresh Frozen Plasma for Activated Clotting Time Monitoring

evidence.reference_title: Coagulation management in endovascular aortic repair in a patient with congenital prekallikrein deficiency: a case report.
evidence.snippet: Intraoperative anticoagulation with heparin and protamine was successfully managed using the activated clotting time measurements after preoperative administration of two units of fresh frozen plasma for prekallikrein replenishment.

evidence.reference_title: Coagulation management in endovascular aortic repair in a patient with congenital prekallikrein deficiency: a case report.
evidence.snippet: Prekallikrein deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive coagulation disorder that prolongs the activated clotting time.

evidence.reference_title: A Rare Cause of Isolated Prolonged Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time: An Overview of Prekallikrein Deficiency and the Contact System.
evidence.snippet: The patient had an uneventful biopsy course after receiving fresh frozen plasma (FFP).

nodes.description: Isolated, markedly prolonged aPTT with a normal prothrombin time and thrombin time. Values in the patients cited here run from about 87 to 146 seconds against upper reference limits near 35 seconds. It corrects fully on mixing with normal plasma, which separates a factor deficiency from an inhibitor, and it shortens on prolonged preincubation with the contact activator, which is the feature that points to prekallikrein rather than to another contact factor.

evidence.reference_title: Severe plasma prekallikrein deficiency: Clinical characteristics, novel KLKB1 mutations, and estimated prevalence.
evidence.snippet: Severe plasma prekallikrein (PK) deficiency is an autosomal-recessive defect characterized by isolated activated partial thromboplastin time prolongation.

evidence.reference_title: Normal thromboelastography with a markedly prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time in severe prekallikrein deficiency: Implications for perioperative hemostatic assessment.
evidence.snippet: The patient had a markedly prolonged aPTT (87.4 s, reference range [RR]: 24.5-34.0 s) with normal PT, thrombin time, and a negative anti-factor Xa assay.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital prekallikrein deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The long partial thromboplastin time is fully corrected by the addition of normal plasma or normal serum and presents the unusual feature of shortening on long incubation times.

nodes.description: Contact activation still happens, but only as fast as factor XII can autoactivate on the surface. The whole laboratory picture follows from this being a kinetic defect rather than an absolute one. In the standard aPTT, with its brief preincubation, too little factor XIIa has formed and the clotting time is grossly prolonged. Extending the preincubation lets autoactivation proceed and the aPTT shortens towards normal, a behaviour seen in prekallikrein-deficient plasma and not in plasma deficient in factor XII, high-molecular-weight kininogen or factor XI, and abolished by an antibody against activated factor XII.
nodes.id: Rate-Limited Factor XII Autoactivation as the Sole Contact Trigger

animal_models.description: Knockout plasma shows the defining kinetic signature of the human defect, a long aPTT and defective contact-activation-induced thrombin generation that partially corrects when incubation is prolonged.
animal_models.name: Plasma prekallikrein-deficient mouse

evidence.reference_title: Prekallikrein deficiency: the characteristic normalization of the severely prolonged aPTT following increased preincubation time is due to autoactivation of factor XII.
evidence.snippet: We conclude that the normalization of a severely prolonged aPTT upon increased preincubation time (PIT), characteristic of PK deficiency, is due to FXII autoactivation.

evidence.reference_title: Prekallikrein deficiency: the characteristic normalization of the severely prolonged aPTT following increased preincubation time is due to autoactivation of factor XII.
evidence.snippet: Addition of OT-2, a monoclonal antibody inhibiting activated FXII, prevented the normalization of aPTT.

evidence.reference_title: A Case of Severe Prekallikrein Deficiency Manifesting as Isolated Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT) Prolongation.
evidence.snippet: Factor XII is able to autoactivate without the presence of kallikrein

nodes.description: Kallikrein liberates bradykinin from high-molecular-weight kininogen, so deficient plasma generates none on contact activation and prekallikrein-null mice have reduced circulating bradykinin. No clinical phenotype in deficient humans has been established for this arm, and bradykinin generation in vivo is clearly not abolished: a patient with complete absence of plasma prekallikrein developed angiotensin-converting-enzyme-inhibitor angioedema, which is bradykinin-mediated, so other enzymes including factor XIIa, plasmin and tissue kallikreins can supply kinin. The weight of this arm is instead established from the opposite direction, because inhibiting kallikrein or lowering prekallikrein treats bradykinin-mediated hereditary angioedema.

evidence.reference_title: Fletcher factor deficiency. A diminished rate of Hageman factor activation caused by absence of prekallikrein with abnormalities of coagulation, fibrinolysis, chemotactic activity, and kinin generation.
evidence.snippet: Fletcher factor-deficient plasma is deficient in prekallikrein and therefore generates no bradykinin upon activation with kaolin.

evidence.reference_title: Reduced thrombosis in Klkb1-/- mice is mediated by increased Mas receptor, prostacyclin, Sirt1, and KLF4 and decreased tissue factor.
evidence.snippet: Klkb1(-/-) mice have reduced plasma BK levels and renal B2R mRNA.

evidence.reference_title: Lisinopril-Induced Angioedema in a Patient with Plasma Prekallikrein Deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Occurrence of angioedema in a patient with complete deficiency of plasma prekallikrein shows other possible enzymes capable of liberating bradykinin such as factor XIIa, plasmin, or tissue kallikreins may also play a role in generating bradykinin during ACE inhibitor therapy

nodes.description: Prekallikrein-null mice are protected across thrombotic and thromboinflammatory challenges while bleeding essentially normally: arterial occlusion is delayed or prevented, and protection extends to models far from coagulation, including brain edema in experimental cerebral malaria and atherosclerotic plaque development. This node is a model-system claim and is named as one, because the corresponding human protection has not been demonstrated. Patients with the deficiency are not protected from thrombosis, which is recorded as an open question rather than resolved here. The platelet and intrinsic-pathway bindings describe the arterial thrombosis arm of this evidence only; the cerebral malaria and atherosclerosis findings are not platelet or intrinsic-pathway readouts.
nodes.id: Reduced Kallikrein-Driven Thromboinflammation in Model Systems

animal_models.description: Arterial occlusion is prevented or delayed across ferric chloride and rose bengal models, and the protection extends to thromboinflammatory and atherosclerotic models. This is the model's distinctive finding and the node is scoped to model systems because of it.
animal_models.name: Plasma prekallikrein-deficient mouse

evidence.reference_title: Effects of plasma kallikrein deficiency on haemostasis and thrombosis in mice: murine ortholog of the Fletcher trait.
evidence.snippet: These studies confirm and extend studies with prekallikrein ASO, and demonstrate that plasma kallikrein deletion prevents occlusive thrombus formation in mice with a minimal role in provoked bleeding.

evidence.reference_title: A comparison of the effects of factor XII deficiency and prekallikrein deficiency on thrombus formation.
evidence.snippet: PK-deficient mice were resistant at 3.5% FeCl3 and partially resistant at 5% FeCl3.

evidence.reference_title: Bradykinin contributes to vasogenic edema in murine experimental cerebral malaria.
evidence.snippet: Prekallikrein-null (Klkb1-/-), prolylcarboxypeptidase hypomorph (Prcpgt/gt), and brain endothelial cell conditional KO of PRCP (Prcpfl/fl Cre) mice with ECM had reduced neurologic deterioration and brain edema.

evidence.reference_title: Ablation of Plasma Prekallikrein Decreases Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol by Stabilizing Low-Density Lipoprotein Receptor and Protects Against Atherosclerosis.
evidence.snippet: Ablation of Klkb1 slowed the progression of atherosclerosis in mice on Apoe-deficient background.

nodes.description: Plasma prekallikrein coagulant activity is severely reduced, typically reported as under 1 to 5 per cent of normal, and this is the finding that defines the disease. Antigen falls in parallel in the cross-reactive-material-negative form and is present but non-functional in the cross-reactive-material-positive form, so antigen alone does not exclude the diagnosis. The bound HPO term names the concentration, while activity is the measurement actually used.

evidence.reference_title: Prekallikrein deficiency: the characteristic normalization of the severely prolonged aPTT following increased preincubation time is due to autoactivation of factor XII.
evidence.snippet: Hereditary PK deficiency was demonstrated by very low PK values in the propositus (PK clotting activity 5%, PK amidolytic activity 5%, PK antigen 2% of normal plasma, respectively) and half normal PK values in his children.

evidence.reference_title: [Severe prekallikrein deficiency due to a compound heterozygosis in the KLKB1-gene].
evidence.snippet: As the cause for the prolonged aPTT we identified a severe prekallikrein deficiency (prekallikrein activity < 1%).

nodes.description: Recurrent missense allele reported in unrelated European and American patients, including as a homozygote in two consecutive unrelated cases with no known consanguinity, and as one half of a compound heterozygous genotype. It was absent from a European population collective, so its recurrence among patients is not explained by high population frequency.

evidence.reference_title: Severe prekallikrein deficiencies due to homozygous C529Y mutations.
evidence.snippet: A homozygous C529Y mutation was identified for both cases, whereas they are unrelated and no consanguineous marriage is known from the patients.

evidence.reference_title: [Severe prekallikrein deficiency due to a compound heterozygosis in the KLKB1-gene].
evidence.snippet: a base exchange Cys 548 (TGC) > Tyr (TAC) in exon 14

nodes.description: Frameshift allele that is common in West African populations and absent from European collectives, and the cause in every genotyped African-ancestry patient reported so far. It is the allele behind the higher estimated prevalence in people of African ancestry.

evidence.reference_title: c.451dupT in KLKB1 is common in Nigerians, confirming a higher prevalence of severe prekallikrein deficiency in Africans compared to Europeans.
evidence.snippet: The frequency of 451dupT was 1.17% in the Nigerian collective (7/600 alleles); none had Cys548Tyr.

evidence.reference_title: c.451dupT in KLKB1 is common in Nigerians, confirming a higher prevalence of severe prekallikrein deficiency in Africans compared to Europeans.
evidence.snippet: To date, all genotyped PK-deficient patients of African ancestry were homozygous for 451dupT.

nodes.description: Homozygous pair of substitutions in the second apple domain of the heavy chain, reported in Japanese patients as PKD Seki. It is the mechanistically distinct class: the apple domains mediate binding to high-molecular-weight kininogen, and recombinant mutant domain binds kininogen poorly, so the defect is in assembly of the prekallikrein-kininogen complex rather than in the catalytic domain. Asn124Ser was subsequently shown to be a common polymorphism, so the pairing matters rather than either substitution alone.

evidence.reference_title: A new type of plasma prekallikrein deficiency associated with homozygosity for Gly104Arg and Asn124Ser in apple domain 2 of the heavy-chain region.
evidence.snippet: We clearly demonstrated that the Gly104Arg-substitution with the Asn124Ser-substitution in A2 reduce the binding activity of A2 to HMWK.

nodes.description: Homozygous nonsense allele truncating the protein within the catalytic domain, a worked example of the dominant truncating class.

evidence.reference_title: Severe prekallikrein deficiency due to a homozygous Trp499Stop nonsense mutation.
evidence.snippet: The mutant allele is predicted to encode a truncated protein lacking half of the catalytic domain of prekallikrein, suggesting that the truncated protein causes prekallikrein deficiency in the patient.
